title: A comment indented under the last entry stays before a member added at the end, in a stream of two documents
notes: The comment is indented more than the key `k`, so it belongs to that entry (see Comments in the edit rules) and the new member goes after it. The comment must not be separated from the entry by the document marker, and must never end up directly after the new literal block scalar, where it would read as the text `# note`.

provenance.reference: Found by comparing random edits of random documents with a plain model while building a lossless document for a Python library.
